Large tables on disk

Source: vignettes/on-disk.Rmd
on-disk.Rmd

A snapshot of GBIF (the Global Biodiversity Information Facility) holds billions of occurrence records in a directory of Parquet files, a column-oriented file format. That is far more than fits in memory. flag_occurrences() accepts such a directory, a single file or a query in place of a data frame. It reads the input in chunks through vectra, the column-store package OccurrenceCleaner uses for tables on disk, and writes the flags to an output directory. This article ends with flags on disk, tallied by group, and a selected subset joined back to its full records. Installation is covered in Get started.

  1. Flag a directory of files into an output directory with flag_occurrences().

  2. Tally what each test flags and each rule removes with tally_flags().

  3. Select flagged records and join them to the full records with flagged_table().

  4. Resume an interrupted run by repeating the call.

Example

Example input

Three files stand in for the parts of a snapshot. They are .vtr files, the on-disk table format of vectra; a directory of Parquet files, a single Parquet, .csv or .tsv file, and a vectra query are read the same way. Each file has 3,000 records with GBIF’s lower-case column names, at random points in a box over western and central Europe. The last record of part 3 is a copy of the first record of part 1 with its own identifier, so the same species and coordinates appear in two files.

Code that writes the three files 
library(OccurrenceCleaner)

set.seed(7)
make_part <- function(n, offset) {
  data.frame(
    gbifid = as.character(offset + seq_len(n)),
    kingdom = sample(c("Animalia", "Plantae", "Fungi"), n, TRUE),
    species = sample(sprintf("sp%02d", 1:30), n, TRUE),
    year = sample(1880:2024, n, TRUE),
    decimallongitude = round(runif(n, -10, 30), 3),
    decimallatitude = round(runif(n, 36, 60), 3))
}
p1 <- make_part(3000, 0)
p2 <- make_part(3000, 3000)
p3 <- make_part(3000, 6000)
p3[3000, -1] <- p1[1, -1]
src <- file.path(tempdir(), "snapshot")
dir.create(src, showWarnings = FALSE)
parts <- list(p1, p2, p3)
for (i in 1:3) {
  path <- file.path(src, sprintf("occurrence-%d.vtr", i))
  vectra::write_vtr(parts[[i]], path)
}
list.files(src)
#> [1] "occurrence-1.vtr" "occurrence-2.vtr" "occurrence-3.vtr"
head(p1, 3)
#>   gbifid kingdom species year decimallongitude decimallatitude
#> 1      1 Plantae    sp10 2009           -1.485          40.392
#> 2      2   Fungi    sp18 1928           -1.194          45.822
#> 3      3   Fungi    sp11 1949            3.827          47.919

Flagging into an output directory

For on-disk input, out names the output directory and keep the columns copied next to the flags for grouping later. The record identifier (gbifid here, set through occ_columns(id = ...)) is kept whenever it is present, so the flags can be joined back to the full records. The run reports its progress as it goes; the messages are folded away here.

The call and its progress messages 
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "flags")
f <- flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = c("kingdom", "year"),
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
#> tests: 12 run; not run, missing input: countryCode, issue, basisOfRecord, establishmentMeans, min_ma, max_ma, datasetKey, range polygons, genus (18 tests)

Without tests, the run covers every test the columns allow. The printed object lists them, and test_plan() gives the reason for each test that did not run:

p <- test_plan(f)
p[!p$run, c("test", "reason")]
#>                        test                            reason
#> 10         country_mismatch           no column `countryCode`
#> 12         issue_coordinate                 no column `issue`
#> 13              issue_taxon                 no column `issue`
#> 14               issue_date                 no column `issue`
#> 15            issue_rounded                 no column `issue`
#> 16             basis_fossil         no column `basisOfRecord`
#> 17             basis_living         no column `basisOfRecord`
#> 18 establishment_introduced    no column `establishmentMeans`
#> 19    establishment_managed    no column `establishmentMeans`
#> 20                age_equal      no column `min_ma`, `max_ma`
#> 22              age_outlier      no column `min_ma`, `max_ma`
#> 23   spatiotemporal_outlier      no column `min_ma`, `max_ma`
#> 24        age_range_outlier      no column `min_ma`, `max_ma`
#> 25             dataset_ddmm            no column `datasetKey`
#> 26          dataset_rounded            no column `datasetKey`
#> 27                    range no range polygons in `gazetteers`
#> 29            sea_nonmarine                 no column `genus`
#> 30              land_marine                 no column `genus`

duplicate and outlier are grouped tests: they compare a record with other records of its key or species anywhere in the input. They run in a group stage that reads the input before the record pass, which the progress messages report.

Tallying from disk

tally_flags() takes the occ_flagged object or the output directory and reads the flag files in chunks. It counts, per group, the records each test flags and each rule removes, without loading the records. A grouping column must have been kept when flagging.

The rule coordinatecleaner holds the same tests as in Choosing a cleaning rule: the default tests of CoordinateCleaner’s clean_coordinates() that need only coordinates and a species, apart from its outlier test.

coordinatecleaner <- c("invalid", "zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid",
                       "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "sea")
t <- tally_flags(out, by = "kingdom", bins = list(year = c(1950, 2000)),
                 rules = list(coordinatecleaner = coordinatecleaner))
sel <- t[, c("kingdom", "year_bin", "n", "flagged_sea", "flagged_capital",
             "removed_coordinatecleaner")]
kingdom year_bin n flagged_sea flagged_capital removed_coordinatecleaner
Animalia <1950 1427 577 3 581
Animalia 1950-2000 1075 428 5 434
Animalia >=2000 513 195 2 197
Fungi <1950 1424 553 4 557
Fungi 1950-2000 1030 414 4 419
Fungi >=2000 493 200 1 202
Plantae <1950 1492 588 1 590
Plantae 1950-2000 1003 397 2 399
Plantae >=2000 543 212 0 212

The sea test flags 40 % of all records, and it accounts for most of the 3,591 records the rule removes: the points were drawn uniformly over a box that includes the Mediterranean, the Bay of Biscay and the North Sea. A grouping column that was not kept is an error that names it:

tally_flags(out, by = "species")
#> Error in `tally_flags()`:
#> ! grouping column(s) not kept in the flag output: species

Selecting and joining flagged records

flagged_table() opens the flag files as one vectra table. vectra verbs run on it lazily and read only what the query needs; vectra::collect() brings the result into memory. A vectra query runs once, so each use starts from a fresh flagged_table().

A filter on a kept column bounds what is collected. For a snapshot, choose one that keeps the result small, such as one class or one region. flags != 0L keeps the records flagged by any test that ran, which here includes duplicate and outlier as well as the tests of the rule above:

fungi <- vectra::filter(flagged_table(out), kingdom == "Fungi", flags != 0L)
flagged <- vectra::collect(fungi)
nrow(flagged)
#> [1] 1252

vectra filters cannot test a single bit of the flag word, so a rule is applied after collecting, with has_flag():

table(removed = has_flag(flagged$flags, coordinatecleaner))
#> removed
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>    74  1178

To attach the flags to the full records, join on the identifier. vectra runs the join on disk, so only the joined rows of the selection are collected:

files <- list.files(src, full.names = TRUE)
records <- do.call(vectra::bind_rows, lapply(files, vectra::tbl))
fungi <- vectra::filter(flagged_table(out), kingdom == "Fungi", flags != 0L)
fungi <- vectra::select(fungi, gbifid, flags)
merged <- vectra::collect(vectra::inner_join(fungi, records, by = "gbifid"))
head(merged[, c("gbifid", "species", "decimallongitude", "flags")])
#>   gbifid species decimallongitude flags
#> 1      4    sp10           27.043   128
#> 2      9    sp02           13.312   128
#> 3     22    sp27           19.655   128
#> 4     25    sp06           28.251   128
#> 5     28    sp15            8.826   128
#> 6     33    sp12           20.121   128

Duplicates across files

The duplicate test compares each record with every record before it in the input order: the files in sorted order and the rows within each file. The copy in the last row of part 3 is flagged and the original in part 1 is not, as they would be in one data frame holding all three parts in that order:

d <- vectra::collect(flagged_table(out))
pair <- d[d$gbifid %in% c(p1$gbifid[1], p3$gbifid[3000]), ]
data.frame(gbifid = pair$gbifid, duplicate = has_flag(pair$flags, "duplicate"))
#>   gbifid duplicate
#> 1      1     FALSE
#> 2   9000      TRUE

Selecting records before flagging

A vectra query can be flagged without writing the subset out first; vectra applies the filter while it scans the file. A query runs once, so it is flagged as one unit, and the grouped tests, which read the input more than once, do not run on it. test_plan() on the result lists them with that reason:

plants <- vectra::filter(vectra::tbl(file.path(src, "occurrence-1.vtr")),
                         kingdom == "Plantae")
h <- flag_occurrences(plants, out = file.path(tempdir(), "flags-plants"),
                      keep = "kingdom", columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"),
                      verbose = FALSE)
h$n
#> [1] 1008
p <- test_plan(h)
p[p$test %in% c("duplicate", "outlier"), c("test", "run", "reason")]
#>         test   run
#> 11 duplicate FALSE
#> 21   outlier FALSE
#>                                                                  reason
#> 11 reads the input more than once; pass a path instead of a vectra_node
#> 21 reads the input more than once; pass a path instead of a vectra_node

Naming a grouped test for a query is an error; flag the file or directory path instead, and select the records afterwards.

Resuming an interrupted run

Each input file is one unit of work, and a finished unit leaves a .done marker in out. Repeating the call skips every finished unit, so a run that was stopped is continued by running the same call again. The messages of the rerun report every unit as skipped:

Messages of the rerun 
f <- flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = c("kingdom", "year"),
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
#> tests: 12 run; not run, missing input: countryCode, issue, basisOfRecord, establishmentMeans, min_ma, max_ma, datasetKey, range polygons, genus (18 tests)
#> progress: record pass, 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 0%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> occurrence-1: done (3000 rows), skipped
#> occurrence-2: done (3000 rows), skipped
#> occurrence-3: done (3000 rows), skipped
#> progress: record pass, 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 100%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: record pass done [0 s]

An interruption during a unit leaves that unit without its marker. Removing a marker by hand has the same effect, and only that unit is flagged again:

Messages after removing one marker 
file.remove(file.path(out, "occurrence-2.done"))
#> [1] TRUE
f <- flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = c("kingdom", "year"),
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
#> tests: 12 run; not run, missing input: countryCode, issue, basisOfRecord, establishmentMeans, min_ma, max_ma, datasetKey, range polygons, genus (18 tests)
#> group tests: reading 3 file(s) (pass 1 of 2)
#> progress: group pass (counts), 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 0%, ETA ~1 s | elapsed 0 s
#> group tests: reading 3 file(s) (pass 2 of 2)
#> progress: group pass (counts), 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 0%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: group pass (counts) done [0 s]
#> progress: group pass (buckets), 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 0%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> group tests: duplicate: 64 bucket(s)
#> progress: group pass (buckets), 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 1%, ETA ~8 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: group pass (buckets) done [0 s]
#> progress: duplicate buckets, 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 1%, ETA ~8 s | elapsed 0 s
#> group tests: outlier: 26 bucket(s)
#> progress: duplicate buckets, 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 2%, ETA ~8 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: duplicate buckets done [0 s]
#> progress: outlier buckets, 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 7 s | run 2%, ETA ~8 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: outlier buckets, 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 89%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: outlier buckets done [0 s]
#> progress: large species, 0 of 0 species | step ETA 0 s | run 89%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: large species, 0 of 0 species | step ETA 0 s | run 89%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: large species done [0 s]
#> group tests: done [0.3 s]
#> progress: record pass, 0 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 89%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> occurrence-1: done (3000 rows), skipped
#> occurrence-2: 3000 rows in 1 part(s) [0 s]
#> occurrence-3: done (3000 rows), skipped
#> progress: record pass, 9,000 of 9,000 rows | step ETA 0 s | run 100%, ETA ~0 s | elapsed 0 s
#> progress: record pass done [0 s]

A unit that is redone has its old part files deleted first. The group stage keeps its state in out/.group until the run finishes. It saves a checkpoint after a file or a bucket of records once five minutes have passed, and at the end of each of its passes, so an interruption there repeats at most the work since the last checkpoint, and an interruption in the record pass reuses its result. Here the run had finished and its group files were deleted, so the redone unit first repeats the group stage. resume = FALSE deletes the earlier output and starts over.

Before writing any output, a run records its configuration: the tests, columns, keep, reference, buffers, test settings, duplicate options, package version, and each input file with its size and modification time. A later call into the same directory must match it, or it stops and names what differs:

flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = "kingdom",
                 columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
#> Error:
#> ! `out` holds flags from a different configuration (keep); use a new directory or resume = FALSE

Sizes and modification times detect a replaced, grown or touched file; they are not a hash of the file contents.

The output directory

The flags are written as .vtr part files. Within a unit, records are read chunk by chunk, flagged and buffered, and a part file is written once at least part_rows rows (two million by default) have accumulated, and at the end of the unit. flags_config.rds holds the configuration record and flags_meta.rds the summary of the finished run:

list.files(out)
#> [1] "flags_config.rds"           "flags_meta.rds"            
#> [3] "occurrence-1.done"          "occurrence-2.done"         
#> [5] "occurrence-3.done"          "part-occurrence-1-0001.vtr"
#> [7] "part-occurrence-2-0001.vtr" "part-occurrence-3-0001.vtr"
#> [9] "progress.txt"
m <- read_flagged(out)
str(m[c("tests", "layout_version", "keep", "n", "units")])
#> List of 5
#>  $ tests         : chr [1:12] "invalid" "zero" "equal" "capital" ...
#>  $ layout_version: int 4
#>  $ keep          : chr [1:2] "kingdom" "year"
#>  $ n             : num 9000
#>  $ units         : chr [1:3] "occurrence-1" "occurrence-2" "occurrence-3"

Progress and threads

A run writes its progress to progress.txt in the output directory, one line overwritten on every report: the step, the items done and their total, the seconds elapsed, the estimated seconds left in the step and in the run, and the share of the run done. A detached run whose console output is buffered can be followed by reading this file. The estimate for the step in progress comes from its own rate; the steps after it are estimated from per-record costs measured on a part of the GBIF snapshot, scaled to the speed of the run so far, so it is rough until the slower steps have started. With verbose = TRUE the same line is printed every minute.

readLines(file.path(out, "progress.txt"))
#> [1] "record 9000 9000 0.4 0.0 0.0 1.0000"

n_threads spreads the exact outlier test and the proximity and point-in-polygon queries over several threads, and the flags are the same for any number of threads. Running on several threads lists the tests that use them and the measured speedup.

Memory and disk

The record pass holds one input chunk, up to part_rows buffered output rows (the identifier, the keep columns and a four-byte flag word per record) and the group-test results for the current block of about one million rows. The group stage holds up to two million bucketed rows before writing them, the record counts per species, the histograms per dataset, the duplicate keys of one bucket (about four million records per bucket on a large input) and the records of one species for the outlier test. On disk it writes up to 24 bytes per record for duplicate, plus the coordinates of the records the outlier test compares; these files are deleted when the run finishes. The Streamed runs section of ?flag_occurrences lists the details.

A GBIF snapshot

GBIF’s Parquet snapshot (the occurrence.parquet directory) names its columns in lower case. They follow Darwin Core, the standard set of field names for biodiversity records, and the case-insensitive defaults of occ_columns() find them. test_plan() on the directory lists the tests the columns allow before anything runs, and keep names the columns a loss analysis groups by:

snapshot <- "gbif_snapshot/occurrence.parquet"
p <- test_plan(snapshot)
p[!p$run, c("test", "reason")]

f <- flag_occurrences(
  snapshot,
  out = "flags",
  keep = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "year",
           "coordinateuncertaintyinmeters"),
  land_scale = 50,
  n_threads = 0)

bins <- list(year = c(1900, 1950, 1970, 1990, 2010),
             coordinateuncertaintyinmeters = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000))
rules <- list(coordinatecleaner = coordinatecleaner,
              with_country = c(coordinatecleaner, "country_mismatch"))
tally_flags(f, by = c("kingdom", "class"), bins = bins, rules = rules)

Read through vectra, the snapshot’s issue column arrives as a string of issue names separated by ;, which the issue tests read directly. With the outlier and dataset tests, which read datasetkey, the group stage reads every file twice before the record pass; with duplicate alone it reads them once. An interruption during the group stage repeats the work since its last checkpoint, and one during the record pass repeats the file in progress.
